citation.title: Fast estimation of ion temperature from EAST charge exchange recombination spectroscopy using neural network
citation.authors: Chai B, Li Y Y, Chen Z, Tao W, Zhou Y X, Mao S F, Luo Z P, Yu Y, Lyu B, Ye M Y
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1088/2058-6272/ab2674 (this paper's own DOI, from the PDF p2 header)

scope_read.pdf_pages: 1-6 (p1 is a publisher cover page; article pp1-5 are PDF pp2-6; Figs 1-4 inspected)
scope_read.limitations: The training shot list, any per-shot training/test separation, the value of the regularization weight lambda, and the learning rate are not reported.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Only two central chords were modeled.
claim_checks.source_finding: Two separate networks with the same architecture were trained, one for chord 10 (R=186.8 cm) and one for chord 7 (R=189.0 cm). The edge CXRS was not modeled.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p5, Sec 3; PDF p3, Sec 2 (chord layout)
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: On EAST, feedforward networks were trained for two central CXRS chords to map individual spectra to ion temperature [Chai2019].
claim_checks.qualification: Core chords only. No pedestal or edge chord was tested.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The networks were trained on conventional-fit labels.
claim_checks.source_finding: The training target is the ion temperature from the two-Gaussian least-squares fit (ACX+PCX). The loss is squared error against that fit plus weight decay. The authors note that systematic CXRS errors persist.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p3, Sec 2, Eqs 1-2; PDF p5, Sec 3, Eq 5; PDF p5, Sec 4
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: The targets were outputs of the conventional fit, so agreement measures emulation of that fit rather than physical accuracy.
claim_checks.qualification: Test MAPE was 2.60% (chord 10) and 3.10% (chord 7) relative to the fit (Fig 4).

claim_checks.proposed_claim: This is an offline feasibility study, not a real-time implementation.
claim_checks.source_finding: Inference timing was measured offline: 95 frames took about 12 ms on a desktop i5-6500 CPU, roughly 0.1 ms per frame, versus about 100 ms per frame for the fit. The authors state that integration and acquisition time must also be considered.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p5, Sec 4; PDF p3, Sec 1; PDF p5, Sec 5
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: In an offline CPU benchmark, network inference took about 0.1 ms per frame, compared with about 100 ms for iterative fitting, which the authors present as a step toward real-time use [Chai2019].
claim_checks.qualification: Real-time relevance is the authors' interpretation (author_claim). No plasma-control-system integration or end-to-end latency was demonstrated.

input_target_timing.inputs: Current-frame CXRS spectrum: 41 background-subtracted, normalized pixels plus the background height and peak height (43 nodes).
input_target_timing.causal_or_offline: Per-frame mapping with no temporal model. Training and evaluation were done offline.
input_target_timing.source_diagnostic_as_input: Yes. The network reads the CXRS spectrum itself, so it is an upstream spectrum reader.
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: Reported conventional-fit Ti is the target. There is no independent physical truth.

validation.split_unit: Training used 1878 frames from 20 shots. Testing used 95 frames from shot #63870.
validation.independent_truth: None. The comparison is against the conventional fit.
validation.unknowns: Whether #63870 was excluded from the 20 training shots is not stated, though it is likely. Test-set MSE was monitored during training to check overfitting, so the test set was not untouched. Campaign diversity and uncertainty intervals are not reported.

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Offline batch inference time on a desktop CPU.
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Real-time deployment, acquisition and integration latency, report arrival times, and feedback use.
runtime_or_deployment.locator: PDF p5, Sec 4; PDF p3, Sec 1

forbidden_inferences: That the method was deployed in real time or used in control
That the network is a temporal or causal nowcaster
That it generalizes to pedestal or edge chords, other devices, or other campaigns
That the reported test MAPE is an untouched holdout estimate
That 0.1 ms is a total latency
That our study implements NN-CES coupling
competing_or_complementary: Complementary. Chai2019 shortens upstream spectrum-to-Ti reading. Our model estimates the current CES report before it is available, using BES/ECEI snapshots and strictly past reports. Faster reading could refresh our anchors but could also reduce the marginal value of nowcasting; whether either effect matters would need validation.
